title: Evaluated K-injective systems are acyclic for finite direct image
statement:
theorem compactSupportEvaluationDirectImage_acyclic
    {Z Y : Scheme.{t}} (p : Z ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ)
    [(compactSupportLevelDirectImage l E p n).Additive]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions (normalizedDVRModules l E Z n)]
    (J : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E Z) ℤ) [J.IsKInjective] :
    IsIso ((compactSupportLevelDirectImage l E p n).rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ
      (((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Z n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj J))

source.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; Evaluated K-injective systems are acyclic for finite direct image

proof.text: Restrict the coefficient-system scalars to the constant integral ring system, and take a K-injective resolution T. Scalar-restriction section acyclicity makes this resolution sectionwise a quasi-isomorphism. The explicit constant-system equivalence with diagrams of integral module sheaves shows that evaluation preserves K-injectives: evaluation has an exact coproduct left adjoint. Evaluate T at n. Given a K-injective resolution r of J_n over the finite ring, restrict r to integral scalars. The K-injective comparison principle factors the evaluated resolution through this restricted r up to homotopy; the resulting comparison is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply scalar-restriction section acyclicity to that comparison, then homotopy invariance and two-out-of-three to conclude that r is sectionwise a quasi-isomorphism. Finite geometric direct image evaluates r on base-changed site objects, hence preserves its quasi-isomorphism by sectionwise detection. Naturality of the derived unit and its invertibility on the K-injective target of r show that the unit at J_n is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; sectionwise scalar-restriction comparison, E6.
